title: A design exploration spreads its mockups across blind, informed and directed lanes
why: Your view, Oct 27: "a lot of design work sometimes prefers a lane or two of totally blank and a lane that gets to see the old and then some in between with directed prompts ... to get a good mix of control and idea between the mockups."
note: Builds on d1 (designer agent, on Opus, on main 2ad85de6), which today draws its options from one brief that sees the current screen. Fix, needs no answer: when the designer explores a screen, it runs a default mix of lanes: one or two blind (blank canvas, never shown the current design), one that sees the current design, and a few in between with directed prompts. Each mockup is labelled with its lane kind, and you cull from the set. The mix is a default, not a hard rule; a brief can change it. Mirrors design-review's blind reviewers A and B. Port: yes; the designer agent installs everywhere. Placed ahead of d9, after d1 and d2 (triage, Oct 27): it shapes every exploration the new designer runs.
